title: Per-class behaviour: the four auth classes each honour their declared contract
asA: platform operator running the service for multiple caller populations
iWant: public, user, admin, and service callers each handled by their class's declared rules
soThat: anonymous traffic, users, administrators, and peer services each get exactly the access and accounting they should

acceptanceCriteria.description: Public endpoints process no auth headers: a request with credentials attached succeeds identically to one without, and no identity is resolved or logged for either.
acceptanceCriteria.when: requests with and without auth headers are submitted
acceptanceCriteria.then: both succeed with identical behaviour and no resolved identity appears in logs or context

acceptanceCriteria.description: Public endpoints are rate-limited under the public class limit even for callers who could authenticate.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a burst of requests to a public endpoint exceeding the public limit
acceptanceCriteria.then: requests beyond the limit receive 429 per the rate-limiting contract

acceptanceCriteria.description: User-class endpoints resolve the caller's identity from a session or bearer token and expose it to the handler; requests without a resolvable identity are rejected with 401.
acceptanceCriteria.when: requests with a valid token, an expired token, and no token are submitted
acceptanceCriteria.then: the valid token resolves an identity available to the handler; the other two receive 401 with the error envelope

acceptanceCriteria.description: Admin-class endpoints require an authenticated identity holding the admin role; an authenticated non-admin receives 403.
acceptanceCriteria.when: an authenticated non-admin and an authenticated admin each call it
acceptanceCriteria.then: the non-admin receives 403 with the error envelope; the admin succeeds

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every admin-class request is audit-logged with the acting identity, the endpoint, the outcome, and the request id.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an admin-class request, successful or rejected
acceptanceCriteria.then: an entry records identity, endpoint, outcome, and request id

acceptanceCriteria.description: Service-class endpoints authenticate the calling service via mTLS or request signature and resolve no user identity.
acceptanceCriteria.when: a correctly signed or mTLS-authenticated peer calls it, and an unauthenticated caller attempts it
acceptanceCriteria.then: the peer succeeds with a service principal and no user identity; the unauthenticated caller receives 401

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every service-class request is audit-logged with the calling service principal, and service-class traffic is counted under its own rate limit separate from user traffic.
acceptanceCriteria.given: service-class traffic at volume alongside user traffic
acceptanceCriteria.when: audit logs and rate-limit counters are inspected
acceptanceCriteria.then: service calls are attributed to the service principal and limited under the service-class limit, independent of user-class counters

acceptanceCriteria.description: A user or admin token presented to a service-class endpoint is rejected: class boundaries do not substitute for each other.
acceptanceCriteria.when: it is presented to a service-class endpoint
acceptanceCriteria.then: the request is rejected with 403 and the error envelope; the admin token grants nothing outside its classes
